description: What is Google AI Mode? It is Gemini's conversational search surface that answers with a generated response. Learn AI Mode vs AI Overviews and how to get cited.
tldr: Google AI Mode is a Gemini-powered, chat-style search surface that answers a query with one generated response — with follow-ups and citations — instead of ten blue links. It became a default search experience in 2026, uses query fan-out to research sub-questions, and rewards answer-first, well-structured, authoritative pages that let AI crawlers in.

sections.heading: What Google AI Mode actually is
body: So what is Google AI Mode? It is Google's full conversational search experience, powered by its Gemini models, that answers your query with a single generated response — often with inline links to its sources — instead of returning the classic list of ten blue links. As of 2026 it has moved from an opt-in experiment to a default surface for a growing share of searches, and it behaves more like a chat than a results page: you ask, it answers, and you can keep asking follow-up questions in the same thread.

The key shift is that AI Mode **synthesizes an answer for you** rather than handing you a list of pages to read. Under the hood it uses a technique called [query fan-out](/blog/what-is-query-fan-out): it silently breaks your one question into many related sub-queries, runs them in parallel, and stitches the best material into a single response. That means the page you land on — if you click at all — is chosen because it answered a sub-question well, not just because it ranked #1 for your exact phrase.

AI Mode is a specific example of a broader shift toward [conversational search](/blog/what-is-conversational-search), where the search box becomes a dialogue. Here is how it lines up against the two surfaces most people already know:

The practical takeaway: AI Mode is generally the most self-contained of the three. It is built to end the search inside the answer, which changes both how often people click and which pages get named as sources.

sections.heading: AI Mode vs AI Overviews: what is the difference?
body: The single most common confusion is treating AI Mode and AI Overviews as the same thing. They are not. **AI Overviews is a box** — a generated summary that sits at the top of an otherwise normal results page, above the usual blue links. You can scroll past it and the classic SERP is still there. **AI Mode is a whole surface** — a dedicated, chat-style search experience where the generated answer *is* the page, and traditional results are secondary or tucked into a side panel.

Put simply: AI Overviews augments the results page; AI Mode replaces it. AI Overviews is generally triggered on specific informational queries; AI Mode is a mode you enter (via a tab or as a default) and stay in across follow-up questions. If you want the deeper mechanics of Overviews specifically, read [how to rank in Google AI Overviews](/blog/how-to-rank-in-google-ai-overviews).
> Both are Gemini-generated and both cite sources — but AI Overviews is a feature bolted onto search, while AI Mode is search reimagined as a conversation.

For content strategy the distinction matters less than it looks. The signals that earn an AI Overview citation — a clear, standalone answer near the top of a well-structured, authoritative page — are the same signals that get you named in AI Mode. Optimizing for one generally optimizes for the other, which is the whole premise of [how AI search engines work](/blog/how-do-ai-search-engines-work).

sections.heading: How AI Mode changes clicks and traffic
body: AI Mode pushes searches further toward **zero-click** outcomes, where the user gets their answer without visiting any website. When a generated response fully satisfies the query — a definition, a comparison, a quick how-to — there is no reason to click through, and impressions that used to become sessions now end on the results surface. This is the central tension of [zero-click search](/blog/what-is-zero-click-search) and it is more pronounced in AI Mode than in a classic SERP.

That does not mean traffic disappears — it means the traffic that remains is more qualified. Clicks in AI Mode generally come from users who want to go deeper than the generated answer: to buy, to verify, to read the primary source, or to follow a specific citation. The click-through rate drops, but the intent behind each remaining click tends to be stronger.

There is also a visibility upside people miss. Because AI Mode fans a query out into sub-questions, your page can be **cited for a sub-topic you never explicitly targeted**. A comprehensive page on "email deliverability" might get named when someone asks AI Mode about "why do my emails land in spam," even though that exact phrase was never your target keyword. Being cited as a source builds authority and brand recognition even on the searches that never convert to a click — which is why measuring AI-search success in 2026 means tracking citations and branded demand, not just raw sessions.

sections.heading: How to show up in Google AI Mode
body: You do not "rank" in AI Mode the way you rank in classic search — you earn a **citation**. The goal shifts from being link #1 to being the passage the model chooses to quote and credit. Four things move that needle, and they are the core of [AI search optimization](/blog/how-to-do-ai-search-optimization):

- **Be answer-first.** Open every section with a direct, self-contained sentence that answers the question, then add detail. AI Mode lifts a passage out of context, so it must survive being read in isolation — the "island test." A paragraph that starts "This depends on many factors..." gives the model nothing to quote.
- **Structure for extraction.** Use question-style headings, short paragraphs, bullet lists, and tables. Clean structure lets the model locate and lift the exact answer to a sub-query.

- **Show authority (E-E-A-T).** Visible author bios, credentials, citations, and first-hand experience signal that your page is a trustworthy source worth crediting. This is the backbone of [generative engine optimization](/blog/what-is-generative-engine-optimization).

- **Let the AI crawlers in.** Confirm your robots.txt does not block Google-Extended, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, or PerplexityBot. If the bots that build AI answers cannot fetch your page, you are invisible in AI Mode no matter how good the content is.

The fastest way to check all four at once is to audit the live URL. Paste it into the [free SEO + GEO audit on the homepage](/) and it flags weak answer-first openers, missing author signals, blocked AI crawlers, and thin structure in a single pass — the exact issues that keep a page out of AI Mode citations.

sections.heading: Can you turn off Google AI Mode?
body: As of 2026, controls over AI Mode vary by region and account, and Google has generally treated it as an increasingly default experience rather than a toggle you fully disable. In some markets you can switch to a classic-results tab or use a "web" filter to see traditional blue links, and browser or search settings sometimes let you avoid landing in AI Mode by default — but expect this to keep shifting as Google iterates.

For searchers who dislike it, the practical workarounds are usually a "Web" results filter, choosing a non-AI search tab where offered, or using an alternative search engine. There is generally no permanent, account-wide off switch that guarantees you never see AI Mode again.

For site owners, the more useful mindset is not "how do I opt out" but "how do I stay visible when my audience is in AI Mode." You cannot control whether your users see AI Mode, but you can control whether your content is citable inside it. Treat AI Mode as the new default context for your keywords, optimize your best pages to be quotable, and measure citations alongside clicks — that is the durable response to a search surface that is not going away.

peopleAlsoAsk.a: Google AI Mode is Google's conversational search experience, powered by its Gemini models, that answers a query with a single generated response instead of a list of ten blue links. It supports follow-up questions in a chat-style thread, cites its sources inline, and uses query fan-out to research sub-questions behind the scenes. As of 2026 it is a default surface for a growing share of searches.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: How is AI Mode different from AI Overviews?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: AI Overviews is a generated box that sits on top of an otherwise normal results page — you can scroll past it to the usual blue links. AI Mode is a whole chat-style surface where the generated answer replaces the results page and supports follow-up questions. In short, AI Overviews augments the SERP; AI Mode reimagines search as a conversation. Both are Gemini-generated and both cite sources.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: How do I rank in Google AI Mode?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: You do not rank in AI Mode so much as earn a citation. Focus on four things: open each section with a direct, standalone answer that survives being read in isolation; structure content with question headings, lists, and tables so it is easy to extract; show visible author and E-E-A-T authority signals; and confirm AI crawlers like GPTBot and Google-Extended are not blocked in robots.txt.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: Does AI Mode reduce website clicks?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: Yes — AI Mode generally increases zero-click searches because the generated answer often satisfies the query without a visit. But the clicks that remain tend to be more qualified, coming from users who want to buy, verify, or read the primary source. AI Mode also cites pages for sub-questions you never targeted directly, so it builds authority and brand recognition even on searches that never convert to a click.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: Can I turn off Google AI Mode?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: As of 2026 there is generally no permanent, account-wide off switch for AI Mode, and controls vary by region. Your practical options are usually a "Web" results filter, choosing a classic-results tab where offered, or switching to an alternative search engine. Google has treated AI Mode as an increasingly default experience, so expect these controls to keep changing over time.

faqs.q: Is Google AI Mode the same as Gemini?
faqs.a: No. Gemini is the underlying AI model, and Gemini is also a standalone chatbot app. Google AI Mode is the search experience built on top of Gemini — it applies those models to live web results, query fan-out, and source citations inside Google Search itself.

faqs.q: Do I need special schema markup to appear in AI Mode?
faqs.a: Schema helps but is not a magic requirement. Clean structured data (Article, FAQ, Product) makes your content easier for models to interpret, yet answer-first writing, clear headings, visible authorship, and unblocked AI crawlers generally matter more for earning an AI Mode citation.

faqs.q: How can I tell if my site is being cited in AI Mode?
faqs.a: Watch for AI-referral traffic in analytics, monitor branded search demand, and manually test your priority queries in AI Mode to see which pages get named. As of 2026 reporting is still immature, so combine manual spot-checks with a GEO audit rather than relying on one dashboard.
